付.meaning: A jacket hangs on a <part>coat hook</part>. A <part>golf club</part> swings in and whacks a sticker onto it, hard. It isn't coming off now: it will <kanji>adhere</kanji> to that jacket forever.
付.on: The sticker ends up stuck to your <sound>fu</sound>ton, and nothing will peel it off.
付.kun: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' you sneeze as you stick a label on the <sound>ke</sound>ttle.

立.meaning: A dot of a head, a wide hat line, two little strokes for legs, and a long line of ground under them. Someone who was slumped in a chair has just jumped up. They <kanji>stand up</kanji>.
立.on: You jump up and a box of <sound>Ritz</sound> crackers tumbles off your lap.
立.kun: You stand up, bow and shout '<sound>Ta</sound>-da!', then sneeze '<sound>tsu</sound>!'

番.meaning: Farmers line up at the <part>rice field</part>, each holding out a <part>paw</part> full of seed. One by one they shake it out over the plots. 'Next!' Everyone waits for their <kanji>turn</kanji>.
番.on: Whoever's turn it is gets a sticky <sound>bun</sound> to eat while they sow.
番.kun: Two swans paddle up for their turn. One sneezes '<sound>tsu</sound>!' and the other gets <sound>ga</sound>rlic stuck in its beak, <sound>ee</sound>k: a pair.

洗.meaning: Muddy legs stride in from the garden, and <part>water drops</part> come flying at them from a hose. '<part>Before</part> you take one more step,' calls a voice, 'scrub!' Soap, a good scrub, and the legs come out pink and clean. Time to <kanji>wash</kanji>.
洗.on: A <sound>sen</sound>try at the door won't let anyone in until they wash.
洗.kun: Under the warm water, the clean legs cheer '<sound>Ah</sound>! <sound>Rah</sound>! <sound>Ooh</sound>!'

使.meaning: A megaphone hangs on a <part>coat hook</part>. An <part>officer</part> grabs it to shout orders, then to call the dog, then to scoop dog food. Megaphone, spoon, shoe: whatever is in reach, he puts it to <kanji>use</kanji>.
使.on: They even use a knight's <sound>shi</sound>eld as a tray for tea and biscuits.
使.kun: Someone sneezes '<sound>Tsu</sound>!', points at two <sound>ca</sound>rs and cries '<sound>Ooh</sound>!' They'll use both.

五.meaning: A number 5 got jammed between a ceiling bar and a floor bar and bent in the middle where it was squashed. It's crooked now, but count it anyway: it's still a <kanji>five</kanji>.
五.on: A swimmer holds up one hand, all fingers out, with a pair of <sound>go</sound>ggles hanging off each one.
五.kun: '<sound>Ee</sound>… <sound>tsu</sound>! <sound>Tsu</sound>!' The swimmer sneezes twice behind foggy goggles, holding up five fingers.

弓.meaning: One stroke bends back and forth three times, like a bow pulled tight with a curl at each tip. Notch an arrow, draw back the string, and let fly: it's a <kanji>bow</kanji>.
弓.on: Out of arrows, the archer fires a pool <sound>cue</sound> from the bow instead.
弓.kun: The archer shoots a <sound>yu</sound>zu off a <sound>mee</sound>rkat's head.
